note: written by twin/video/floorspace.py: four layouts of the 3-D lab's equipment, and the Shuttles' capacity laid out flat (design layouts, not built labs)

rows.name: conventional
rows.title: Conventional lab
notes: Zones along a 6 ft corridor; each zone's back row against its far wall, its front row against the corridor wall, a 5 ft aisle between them.

rows.name: flat
rows.title: Automated, same floor plan
notes: 4 mobile manipulators; 24 docking targets; 5 fixed arms, each with a sample rack; 2 chargers. A docked MiR250 (580 mm wide) leaves 0.94 m of a 5 ft aisle: less than the 1.45 m one needs to drive by, so robots wait in the aisles.

rows.name: robots
rows.title: Automated, laid out for robots
notes: 18 tray-sized bench positions (18 with today's trays): 2 where the Shuttles stood, facing the MiR aisle; 16 in 4 rows of up to 4, 2 one-way 1.45 m MiR aisles with an 838 mm dock lane each side, cross-aisles at both ends; the floor machines as in the vertical lab.

rows.name: vertical
rows.title: Vertical lab
notes: North row: glovebox, atomizer, sieving cell, two Shuttles, LPBF. South row: two Instrons, three chargers, fume hood, DED, wire EDM, packaging. East end: EOS M 400-4 and Meltio cell (no MiR dock).

empty_unit.note: an empty 9.15 m unit at the 750 mm span; the 493 mm under the access table takes short stores only (the plan has one or two there)

trays.note: each tray also carries its UPS, cameras, air monitor, dock plate and lines

robots.verdict: more room: a docked MiR250 (580 mm wide) leaves 944 mm of a 5 ft aisle, under the 1,450 mm one needs to drive by; facing rows a robot can serve and pass along need 838 + 1,450 + 838 = 3,126 mm between them, twice the 1,524 mm aisle

machine_block.note: the 12 floor machines in the vertical lab's two rows along its 3.0 m MiR aisle, with their 0.6 m service space, three chargers and their docks, without the Shuttles: the same in the vertical lab and both flat automated layouts
